title: Universal density and geometric reducedness of a separable-point closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure (an algebraic separable extension which is separably closed), and let $Z$ be a locally finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $T\subset Z(k^{\mathrm{sep}})$ be stable under every $k$-automorphism of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, where a point is a $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k^{\mathrm{sep}}\to Z$. Let $Y\hookrightarrow Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closure of the images of $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. For every field extension $L/k$ inside a common algebraically closed overfield containing $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $Y_L$ is reduced. The induced points of $T$ are schematically dense in $Y_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$: on every open affine, a function vanishing at all those points in that affine is zero. For every integer $m\geq1$, the tuples in $T^m$ are schematically dense in $(Y_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}})^m$, and remain so after any field extension of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Here $Y_L$ and the products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], reduced means all local rings have no nonzero nilpotents, and schematic density means precisely the stated test on regular functions. The empty set $T$ is allowed.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Lemma 4, printed p.67, geometric reducedness from schematic density of separable points; coefficient-basis and product-density extension of this argument by O4, used in 7.1 Lemma 4. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Put $K=k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Every $t\in T$ factors through $Y$: on an affine of $Z$, the ideal of the reduced closure consists of functions vanishing on that closure, so its image under $t$ is zero in the field $K$, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The images of these factorizations are dense in $Y$ by the definition of closure. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be any affine open of $Y$, and let $T_U$ be the points landing in $U$. Their images are dense in $U$, since every nonempty open of $U$ is open in $Y$ and meets $T$. If $b\in B$ evaluates to zero at every $t\in T_U$, its zero locus contains this dense set and hence is all of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] and [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $b$ lies in $\sqrt{(0)}$. The ring $B$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], because $Y$ is reduced, so $b=0$. Thus $B\to K^{T_U}$, $b\mapsto(t(b))_t$, is injective.

For this $U$, let $W$ be the kernel of evaluation $B\otimes_kK\to K^{T_U}$, with $(b\otimes c)(t)=t(b)c$. It is a $K$-linear subspace. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(K)$ and $f\in W$, evaluation gives $(\sigma f)(t)=\sigma(f(\sigma^{-1}t))=0$. Here $\sigma^{-1}t\in T_U$: $T$ is stable and $\sigma$ fixes the underlying image in the $k$-scheme $Y$, hence preserves membership in $U$. Thus $W$ is stable under every $\sigma$. The extension $K/k$ is algebraic normal separable by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], so [lem-sfb-galois-stable-subspace-descent], with $M=B$, says $W=W_0\otimes_kK$, where $W_0=\{b:b\otimes1\in W\}$. Step 1 gives $W_0=0$, whence $W=0$. In particular evaluation on $T_U$ is injective on $B_K=B\otimes_kK$.

source.place: Appendix A.64–A.65, printed pp.580–581: invariant subspaces of scalar extensions; applied to the evaluation kernel. The application is written by Q160.

proof.text: Let $E/K$ be any field extension. Choose a $K$-basis $(e_j)$ of $E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector]. A tensor $f\in B_K\otimes_KE$ has a finite expression $f=\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$, after expanding its finitely many scalar coefficients in that basis. If it vanishes at every induced $E$-point of $T_U$, then $\sum_j b_j(t)e_j=0$ for each $t$. The numbers $b_j(t)$ lie in $K$, so independence of the $e_j$ gives $b_j(t)=0$ for all $j,t$. Step 2 gives $b_j=0$ and $f=0$. Thus $B_K\otimes_KE\to E^{T_U}$ is injective for every $E/K$, including $E=K$. We used only finite sums; tensor bilinearity and the tower identification are [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension].

source.place: Tensor products Tag 00CV and associativity Tag 00D0; coefficient-basis argument written by Q160, extending the density argument of BLR 3.3 Lemma 4.

proof.text: Fix an allowed $L/k$ and a common algebraically closed overfield $E$ containing $L$ and $K$ with compatible $k$-embeddings. For each affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$, step 3 embeds $B\otimes_kE\cong B_K\otimes_KE$ into $E^{T_U}$. A nilpotent has zero image in each field $E$, hence is zero by injectivity. Also $B\otimes_kL\to(B\otimes_kL)\otimes_LE\cong B\otimes_kE$ is injective: choose an $L$-basis of $B\otimes_kL$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector]; its scalar-extended vectors are an $E$-basis by [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], so a nonzero finite coordinate vector stays nonzero. Therefore $B\otimes_kL$ is reduced too. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], the $U_L=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kL)$ form an affine open cover of $Y_L$. Each is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]; every point of $Y_L$ has its local ring in one such open, proving that $Y_L$ is reduced.

source.place: Tags 01I4/01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes/lemma-fibre-product-affines), 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01J2; coefficient proof of the geometric-reducedness argument of BLR 3.3 Lemma 4, printed p.67.

proof.text: For $m\ge1$ choose affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $Y$ and set $A_i=B_i\otimes_kK$. Evaluation $A_i\to K^{T_{U_i}}$ is injective by step 2. We prove by induction that $C_m=A_1\otimes_K\cdots\otimes_KA_m$ is detected by $\prod_iT_{U_i}$. The case $m=1$ is step 2. For the induction step, choose a $K$-basis $(c_j)$ of $A_m$, using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector], and write $f=\sum_j a_j\otimes c_j$, $a_j\in C_{m-1}$, with finite support. Suppose all tuple evaluations of $f$ vanish. Fix a tuple $s$ in the first $m-1$ sets. The element $\sum_j a_j(s)c_j\in A_m$ evaluates to zero at every $t_m\in T_{U_m}$, so it is zero. Independence gives $a_j(s)=0$. Varying $s$ and using the induction hypothesis gives $a_j=0$, hence $f=0$. For any $E/K$, apply the coefficient-basis argument of step 3 to this injective evaluation on $C_m$: writing a tensor as $\sum_j f_j\otimes e_j$ in a $K$-basis of $E$ shows that its vanishing at all induced tuples forces every $f_j$ to vanish, hence to be zero. Thus $C_m\otimes_KE\to E^{\prod_iT_{U_i}}$ is injective. These tensor expressions use [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension].

source.place: Tensor products Tag 00CV and associativity Tag 00D0; finite tensor induction and coefficient expansion written by Q160, making explicit the product-density extension in the item source.

proof.text: The affine products $(U_1)_K\times_K\cdots\times_K(U_m)_K$, and their $E$-base changes, form open covers of $(Y_K)^m$ and $((Y_K)^m)_E$, with coordinate rings $C_m$ and $C_m\otimes_KE$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. It remains to justify the density test on an arbitrary affine open, rather than only on these cover members. For any ring $A$ with an injective evaluation $A\to F^S$ at $F$-rational points, suppose $b/g^r\in A_g$ vanishes at every $s\in S$ with $g(s)\ne0$. Then $b(s)=0$ at those points, and $g(s)b(s)=0$ at all other points as well. Thus $gb$ evaluates to zero everywhere, so $gb=0$ and $b/g^r=0$ in $A_g$. This proves injectivity on every principal open of each cover member. The principal opens form a basis and their section rings are the localizations, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Any open affine of the product is covered by such principal opens contained in it; a section vanishing at its $T^m$ points restricts to zero on each, hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. This proves every requested schematic-density assertion, including $m=1$ over $K$ and arbitrary $E/K$.

source.place: Tags 01I4, 01JQ, 01JR and the structure sheaf on principal opens; localization-and-sheaf argument written by Q160.

proof.text: If $T=\varnothing$, its image closure is empty and $Y$ is the empty reduced induced closed subscheme by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Every field base change is empty and every positive power is empty; the section ring on the empty open is the zero ring, so reducedness and the vanishing tests hold. More generally any empty $T_U$ or empty affine factor in the preceding arguments forces its coordinate ring to be zero by step 1 or step 2; hence the injections, coefficient calculations and induction also include these cases. No quasi-compactness or separatedness of $Z$ has been used.
